toc.title: Reading, answering, shortcuts and staying calm

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. SQS: Simple Queue Service; SNS: Simple Notification Service; AZ: Availability Zone; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; IAM: Identity and Access Management; KMS: Key Management Service; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; RDS: Relational Database Service; ALB: Application Load Balancer

  • Pace the 65 questions in 130 minutes with checkpoints
  • Use a four-step method: read, predict, eliminate, confirm
  • Handle multiple-response questions, qualifier words and look-alike traps
  • Plan your final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake

2Reading, answering, shortcuts and staying calm

Running case

Lantern and Loom's Mock Exam

  • A teammate sat a practice exam and finished just under the pass mark
  • The review showed lost points, not lost knowledge: misread questions, look-alike services and blank answers
  • The course content is covered; now technique has to match it
  • Your job: turn what you know into points

The Exam Clock Beyond the guide

  • 65 questions in 130 minutes is about 2 minutes each
  • Aim for about 100 seconds on a first pass; the spare time is for long scenarios and review
  • Use checkpoints as the latest you should reach: question 20 by minute 40, 40 by 80, 65 by 120
  • 15 questions are unscored and you cannot tell which, so treat every one as real

Exam tip

If you are behind at a checkpoint, answer quickly and move on; a blank always scores zero.

Read for the Requirement Beyond the guide

  • Read the last line first: it holds what is being asked (a tip from AWS's own certification blog)
  • Then read the scenario and underline the requirement words: most cost-effective, least operational overhead, highest availability, most secure
  • Note the verb: encrypt, decouple, cache, fail over, migrate, restrict
  • Note the constraint: Region, downtime allowed, budget, existing skills
  • Predict the answer before you look at the options
Exam tip

The scenario is the story; the last line is the test.

A Four-Step Answer Method Beyond the guide

  • Read: the last line first, then the scenario
  • Predict: name the service or pattern before you see the options
  • Eliminate: remove the options that are clearly wrong
  • Confirm: match the requirement word and the verb to what is left

Exam tip

A prediction stops a plausible distractor from pulling you off course.

Eliminating Distractors Beyond the guide

  • Distractors are real services that sound plausible, so ask why each one fails
  • Wrong job: it does something else (SQS buffers; SNS fans out)
  • Wrong scope: a Multi-AZ fix for a Region failure, or the reverse
  • Over-engineered: Multi-Region active-active when a backup meets the goal
  • Self-managed: EC2 with custom code when a managed service fits
  • Half true: one clause fits and another does not
  • Words such as always and never deserve a second look
Exam tip

Remove two of four options and a guess is right half the time.

Multiple-Response Questions Beyond the guide

  • SAA-C03 has two question types: multiple choice (one correct, three distractors) and multiple response (two or more correct among five or more options)
  • The question tells you how many to choose, such as Select TWO
  • Judge each option on its own, true or false against the question, then count
  • Choose exactly the number asked
  • If three options fit, reread for the qualifier that rules one out
Exam tip

Two correct answers are often one for each part of the requirement.

Qualifier Words Steer the Answer Beyond the guide

If the question says… Think…
Most cost-effective Spot, Savings Plans, lifecycle rules, serverless, right-sizing, gateway endpoints
Least operational overhead Managed and serverless: Lambda, Fargate, Aurora, SQS
Highest availability Multi-AZ, Auto Scaling, Multi-Region only if the Region must survive
Most secure, least privilege IAM roles, KMS, private subnets, narrow policies
Lowest latency CloudFront, Global Accelerator, caches, closer Region
Decouple SQS, SNS, EventBridge
Minimal downtime Blue/green, replication, Multi-AZ failover
Exam tip

Underline the qualifier: it picks one correct answer from several that work.

Architecture Question Shortcuts

The symptom Think…
Spiky load, dropped requests Queue it, Auto Scaling
Slow worldwide users CloudFront or Global Accelerator
Read-heavy database Read replicas, caching
Data in S3 must be locked down Bucket policy, Block Public Access, KMS, VPC endpoint
Single AZ failure takes it down Multi-AZ and Auto Scaling
Who did it, what changed CloudTrail; Config
Bill too high Right-size, Savings Plans, lifecycle, endpoints
Exam tip

Most questions are pattern matching: name the symptom first, then the fix.

Choosing Between Two Valid Answers Beyond the guide

  • When two answers both work, ask which one is simpler, managed and cheaper
  • Prefer serverless and managed services over EC2 you operate
  • Prefer IAM roles over access keys, and least privilege over broad access
  • Prefer the design that meets the stated goal and no more: extra Regions and tiers cost money
  • Check the scope: account, Region, AZ or instance
  • Make sure nothing in the option breaks a stated constraint
Exam tip

The best answer meets every stated requirement with the least effort and cost.

When You Are Unsure Beyond the guide

  • Never leave a question blank: the guide says an unanswered question counts as incorrect and a guess has no penalty
  • Eliminate first, then choose between what is left
  • When two answers fit, prefer the one that is managed, least privilege and simplest
  • Change an answer only when you find a specific reason
  • If the screen lets you mark a question to revisit, use it for hard ones, and check the exam tutorial
Exam tip

A blank always scores zero; a guess might not.

3Preparation and practice

Your Final Week Beyond the guide

When Do this
Seven days out Read the current exam guide again and check for changes
Six to four days out Redo the questions for your two weakest domains; write your own look-alike notes
Three days out Take a timed run of about 65 questions in 130 minutes; AWS offers practice question sets
Two days out Read module 15 once, then say the lists aloud
The day before A light review, a good night's sleep and your exam-day logistics
Exam tip

Practice under the clock: pace is a skill, and it improves with repetition.

Exam Day and Afterwards [Verify live]

  • Delivery: at a Pearson VUE test center or online with a proctor; read the provider's rules
  • Fee: USD 150; a pass is valid for 3 years
  • Results: posted to your AWS Certification Account within five business days after the exam, unless held for review
  • If you do not pass: wait 14 calendar days; there is no limit on attempts and each one needs the full fee
  • If you pass: you cannot retake the same exam for two years
  • As of 5 November 2026: AWS may change fees and policies, so read its pages before you book
Exam tip

Policies and fees change; check AWS's certification pages before you book.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom's Mock Exam

What went wrong Technique to apply
Ran short of time in the last ten questions Checkpoints: question 20 by minute 40, 40 by minute 80
Chose Multi-Region for "highest availability" in one Region Read the scope: Multi-AZ meets an AZ failure
Picked one answer in a "Select TWO" question Judge each option and choose exactly two
Built a custom queue on EC2 Read the qualifier: least overhead means managed
Left three questions blank Answer every one: there is no penalty
Chose SNS to buffer a spike Read the verb: buffering is SQS
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Lantern and Loom's order intake drops requests during sales. The team wants to absorb the spikes with the least operational overhead. Which solution fits best?

  • AA fleet of EC2 instances that poll a database table for new orders
  • BCustom retry code on one large EC2 instance
  • CAn Amazon SQS queue ahead of Lambda consumers
  • DSelf-managed RabbitMQ on EC2 instances
Show the answer

Answer: C. The requirement words are absorb spikes and least operational overhead. SQS buffers the orders and Lambda scales its consumers with no servers. Polling a table, custom retry code and a self-managed broker all add operations.

S2Lantern and Loom's web tier is one EC2 instance, and its database is a single-AZ RDS instance. The goal is to survive the loss of one Availability Zone with the least change. Which TWO actions help? (Select TWO.)

  • ATurn on Multi-AZ for the database
  • BRun the web tier in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an ALB
  • CMove to a larger instance type in the same zone
  • DAdd a read replica in the same zone
  • EIncrease the backup retention period
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Multi-AZ gives the database a standby in another zone, and an Auto Scaling group across zones behind a load balancer removes the web tier's single point of failure. The other options do not survive a zone loss.

S3A Lambda function must read objects from one S3 bucket and nothing else. Which approach follows the exam's least-privilege preference?

  • AEmbed a long-term access key in the function code
  • BGive the function an administrator role to avoid permission errors
  • CMake the bucket public so the function needs no credentials
  • DAttach a role that allows read access to only that bucket
Show the answer

Answer: D. An execution role scoped to read one bucket gives temporary credentials and the narrowest permission. Embedded keys, administrator access and a public bucket all break least privilege.

S4With six minutes left, a candidate has four questions unanswered and is unsure of each. Based on the exam guide's scoring rules, what should they do?

  • ALeave all four blank, because wrong answers lower the whole score
  • BAnswer all four, since a blank scores zero and a guess has no penalty
  • CAnswer only the two that feel most likely, and leave the other two blank
  • DSpend the remaining time rechecking earlier answers instead of guessing
Show the answer

Answer: B. The exam guide says unanswered questions are scored as incorrect and there is no penalty for guessing. A guess can only help; a blank always scores zero.

S5Which TWO statements about SAA-C03 scoring are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AWrong answers subtract points from the score
  • BEach domain must be passed separately
  • CThe exam has 50 scored and 15 unscored questions, and the unscored ones are not identified
  • DA scaled score of 500 is the minimum to pass
  • EUnanswered questions are scored as incorrect
Show the answer

Answer: C, E. The exam includes 50 scored and 15 unscored questions that are not identified, and unanswered questions count as incorrect. Guessing has no penalty, scoring is compensatory across domains, and the minimum passing score is 720.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Pace 65 questions, 130 minutes, about 2 minutes each, with checkpoints
Method read the last line, predict, eliminate, confirm
Types multiple choice and multiple response
Traps look-alike services, qualifier words, wrong scope and over-engineering
Unsure never leave a blank; there is no penalty for guessing
Plan a final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake after 14 days
